name: The Eyrie Vineyards

sources.title: Valley View Winery collection, 2026 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Troon Vineyard

sources.title: Troon Vineyard collection, 2026 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

summary: Eola-Amity Hills winery founded in 1992 by Paul and Eileen Gerrie on the abandoned Pellier Winery site and named after their children Christine and Tom.

Lingua Franca collection, 2026 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

summary: Dundee winery established in fall 1999 by John and Karen Bergström and their son Josh, with estate vineyards in the Dundee Hills, Ribbon Ridge and Chehalem Mountains.

sources.title: BergströM Wines collection, 2025 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Domaine Serene
summary: Dundee Hills estate founded in 1989 by Ken and Grace Evenstad, with a first commercial vintage in 1990. Ken Wright was its first winemaker.

summary: Oregon wine company founded by Bill and Deb Hatcher, Cheryl Francis and Sam Tannahill, who took over Rex Hill when its founders retired. Ste. Michelle Wine Estates acquired A to Z and Rex Hill in 2022.

summary: Winery west of Roseburg founded by Richard Sommer in 1961, described as Oregon's first post-Prohibition estate winery and the site of the state's first Pinot noir plantings. Sold in 2003 to Dyson and Susan DeMara.

summary: Vineyard, nursery and winery run by Charles and Shirley Coury near Forest Grove from 1965 until financial strain forced a sale in 1978. Milan and Jean Stoyanov bought the property in 1992 and renamed it David Hill Vineyards & Winery.

summary: Dundee winery founded by Dick Erath, which made its first commercial wine in 1972 and traded as Knudsen Erath from 1975 to 1988. Bought by Ste. Michelle Wine Estates in 2006.

summary: Partnership between grower Cal Knudsen and winemaker Dick Erath, established in 1975 and described as the first commercial winery in the Dundee Hills. The partners separated in 1988 and Erath continued under his own name.

sources.title: Adelsheim Vineyard collection (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Sokol Blosser Winery
summary: Founded by Bill Blosser and Susan Sokol Blosser in 1971 in what is now the Dundee Hills AVA, with a first vintage in 1977. Opened a tasting room in 1978 and is now led by the second generation.

sources.title: Amity Vineyards collection, 2026 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

summary: Family-owned winery founded in 1974 by Pat and Joe Campbell near Gaston, the first winery in what is now the Yamhill-Carlton appellation.

sources.title: Joe Campbell, Pioneering Willamette Valley Winemaker, Dies at 87 (Wine Spectator)
Elk Cove Vineyards collection, 2023 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

summary: Established in 1973 near Forest Grove by Bill Fuller and Bill Malkmus. Owned by Willamette Valley Vineyards since 1997 and now known as Tualatin Estate Vineyard.

sources.title: Tualatin Vineyards collection, 2015 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: St. Innocent Winery
summary: Winery founded by Mark Vlossak in 1988, known for single-vineyard wines from sites including Freedom Hill, Temperance Hill, Shea and Momtazi. It operated at Zenith Vineyard from 2006 and moved in 2019 to its Enchanted Way Vineyard in the South Salem Hills.

sources.title: St. Innocent Winery collection, 2019 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

summary: Dundee winery founded in 1984 by John Paul with partners including his wife Teri Wadsworth and Bill and Julia Wayne of Abbey Ridge Vineyard. Its estate vineyard, Clos Electrique, surrounds the winery.

sources.title: Cameron Winery collection, 2024 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

summary: Dundee Hills winery established in 1993 by Gary Andrus and Nancy Andrus, the founders of Pine Ridge Vineyards in Napa. Andrus sold it in 2001 and it is now owned by Crimson Wine Group.

summary: Doug Tunnell's 40-acre estate in the Ribbon Ridge AVA, certified organic since 1990 and Demeter-certified biodynamic since 2005. Pinot noir was planted in 1990 and the first vintage was 1993; all fruit is estate grown.

summary: Winery founded in 1993 by Amy Wesselman and David Autrey, its name a blend of their surnames. It began with purchased fruit and now also farms 22 acres at its Oracle Vineyard in the Dundee Hills, next to Abbey Ridge.

summary: Shared winemaking facility in Carlton opened in 2002 by Eric Hamacher, Luisa Ponzi and Ned and Kirsten Lumpkin, after Oregon law changed to let several independent wineries share one facility. Early tenants included Hamacher Wines, Lazy River and Andrew Rich.

name: Maison Louis Jadot
summary: Burgundy wine house, launched in 1859. In 2013 it bought the Résonance Vineyard in Yamhill-Carlton, its first project outside France, and later added a Dundee Hills site.

name: Résonance

name: Domaine Méo-Camuzet
summary: Côte d'Or domaine owned and run by Jean-Nicolas Méo, co-founder of Oregon's Nicolas-Jay.

name: Gran Moraine
summary: Jackson Family Wines' Yamhill-Carlton label, based on the 200-acre Gran Moraine Vineyard the company acquired in May 2013. It is made at the former Soléna Estate winery near Yamhill, which Jackson also bought.

sources.title: Foley Family Wines Buys Oregon's The Four Graces (Wine Spectator)

summary: Bill Foley's wine company, an active buyer of wineries since 1996. The Four Graces, bought in 2014, was its first Oregon acquisition.

sources.title: Italian wine group acquires Dundee Hills vineyard from Coppola-owned Domaine Lumineux (Newsberg)

name: Domaine Lumineux

sources.title: Italian wine group acquires Dundee Hills vineyard from Coppola-owned Domaine Lumineux (Newsberg)

sources.title: Exclusive: Silver Oak Owners Buy Oregon Vineyard from Dick Erath (Wine Spectator)

name: Chapter 24 Vineyards
summary: Willamette Valley Pinot noir producer launched in 2012 by Mark Tarlov after he left Evening Land, with Burgundy vigneron Louis-Michel Liger-Belair as partner and consultant. In 2016 its owners bought the Witness Tree property in the Eola-Amity Hills.

sources.title: Chapter 24 Wines Purchases Witness Tree and Five Other Vineyards in Oregon's Willamette Valley (Wine Spectator)

name: Maison Bleue
summary: Winery founded by Jon and Amy Meuret in Washington in 2007 and later based in Walla Walla. Willamette Valley Vineyards bought the brand in January 2018 and set aside 15 acres of its land in The Rocks District of Milton-Freewater for a Maison Bleue estate vineyard.

sources.title: Oregon's Willamette Valley Vineyards Buys Maison Bleue in Walla Walla Valley (Wine Spectator)

sources.title: Phelps Creek Vineyards collection, 2014 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Domaine Marc Roy
summary: Family domaine in Gevrey-Chambertin, Burgundy, where Alexandrine Roy is the fourth-generation winemaker.

name: Watermill Winery
summary: Milton-Freewater winery established in 2005 by the Brown family, third-generation apple growers, in a renovated 1944 pea processing plant. The Foreman and Kleinman families became partners in 2017.

summary: Milton-Freewater winery founded in 2001 by Cecil and Marilyn Zerba after 20 years in the nursery business. Its estate vineyards include Dad's Vineyard, Cockburn Ranch and Winesap Road Vineyard in The Rocks District.

summary: Rogue Valley estate at Gold Hill on the former Del Rio pear orchard, which Californians Lee and Margaret Traynham bought in 1997 and converted to wine grapes with Rob and Jolee Wallace. sources.title: Day Wines collection, 2019 (Oregon Wine History Archive)

name: Walter Scott Wines
summary: Eola-Amity Hills producer of Chardonnay and Pinot noir started in 2008 by Ken Pahlow and Erica Landon. Its winery was built next to Justice Vineyard in time for the 2014 vintage.

sources.title: Walter Scott Wines collection, 2019 (Oregon Wine History Archive)
